import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_73/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_73/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_73_0 and Source3_73_1 on "city"
# According to operation history: JOIN : [["Source3_73_0", "Source3_73_1"], ["city", "city"]]
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, left_on="city", right_on="city", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by = ["Source3_73_0.city", "Source3_73_0.type"], aggregations = [ "avg(Source3_73_1.fare)" ]
# Group by city and type from Source3_73_0 (which are columns 'city' and 'type' in df_joined)
# Aggregate average fare from Source3_73_1 (column 'fare' in df_joined)
df_grouped = (
    df_joined
    .groupby(["city", "type"], as_index=False)
    .agg(fare=("fare", "mean"))
)

# Ensure the column order and types match the target schema: ['city': string, 'type': string, 'fare': float]
df_grouped = df_grouped.astype({"city": str, "type": str, "fare": float})

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_73/target_multisource.csv"
df_grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
